sources.entry: MacClean - Free local Mac disk cleaner that lets you review WeChat media, System Data, and Xcode or AI caches before deleting. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jinglings/MacClean) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: MacClean is a native macOS disk analysis, cleanup, and system maintenance tool for Apple silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 14 or later.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes MacClean as a native macOS app for disk analysis, cleanup, and system maintenance. The awesome-mac listing says it lets users review WeChat media, System Data, and Xcode or AI caches before deleting them. Scanning and cleaning run locally on the machine. Dangerous operations require confirmation, and path protection and system permission checks are part of the app. Anonymous usage statistics are off by default and can be enabled in settings. The README also notes that the website and backend live in a web/ directory. Build instructions cover opening the Xcode project and building from the command line with DEVELOPER_DIR pointed at a full Xcode install.
use_cases: free up disk space on a Mac
clear AI model caches on macOS
how_to_run: Select the MacClean scheme and build.
For command-line builds, set DEVELOPER_DIR to a full Xcode installation.
See RELEASE.md for release steps and current signing limitations.
stack: web/ directory for website and backend
notable: Native macOS app supporting Apple silicon and Intel
Lets users review WeChat media, System Data, and Xcode or AI caches before deletion
Scanning and cleaning run locally; anonymous analytics are opt-in and off by default
Free for personal and internal business use from version 1.6, with all features unlocked and no trial or device limits
Path protection and dangerous-action confirmations apply regardless of license
caveats: Commercial resale or integration into paid products requires a separate paid commercial license.
Source-available community license, not an OSI-approved open source license.
README notes current signing limitations documented in RELEASE.md.
